title: Dashboard signal workbench + session reconstruction cookbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working cookbook for building compact, cost-conscious dashboards and reliable session-reconstruction traces for tokenized inference flows. Goal: reduce mean time to diagnose (MTTD) for latency regressions and quality fallbacks while keeping dashboard query cost low.

Why a separate workbench?
- Observability for inference is noisy (token-level churn, many micro-spans). We need a minimal, repeatable set of panels and trace anchors that let an engineer go from alert -> root cause in <10 minutes.
- Focus on three modes: incident triage, regression hunting (quality/latency drifting), and capacity / cost checks.

Quick sketch: three-pane workbench
1) Incident triage (top-left): single-row summary for impacted tenants + 5 minute SLO delta, error rate, median p95 latency by route.
2) Session reconstruction (top-right): compact span timeline for a single request (trace anchor + flattened spans).
3) Probe & cohort (bottom): cohort heatmap of latency by input-size bucket + cost estimate (tokens * cost/unit).

Metric catalog (compact, one-line definitions)
- request.count | intent: traffic volume | unit: count | agg: sum/1m | owner: router-team | alert: sudden drop >30% vs baseline 30m
- request.error_rate | intent: infra & model errors | unit: ratio | agg: errors/requests 1m | owner: runtime-team | alert: >1% sustained 5m or spike x5
- latency.end_to_end_p50/p95 | intent: user-perceived latency | unit: ms | agg: approxQuantile(50/95) over 1m | owner: obs-team | alert: p95 > target + 50ms for 3 consecutive windows
- latency.decode_ms | intent: model decode time | unit: ms | agg: p95 | owner: serving-runtime | alert: sustained increase vs baseline
- latency.queue_ms | intent: time waiting in scheduler/batching | unit: ms | agg: p95 | owner: serving-runtime | note: correlate with batch.size
- kvcache.hit_rate | intent: cache effectiveness | unit: ratio | agg: sum(hits)/sum(lookups) 5m | owner: runtime-cache
- tokens.generated_per_request | intent: token economics and cost | unit: tokens | agg: avg 5m | owner: billing/optimize | alert: sudden increase per route
- fallback.model_rate | intent: frequency of fallback to smaller/safer model | unit: ratio | agg: sum(fallbacks)/sum(requests) 5m | owner: rollout-team | alert: trend up after deploy

Span/trace anchor design (keep traces skinny):
- Mandatory top-level attributes: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), route_name, model_variant, token_count_estimate, sample_trigger (enum: baseline|high-latency|error|investigation)
- Minimal span names (consistent naming): http.recv -> router.route -> scheduler.batch_wait -> runtime.invoke -> runtime.decode -> kv.cache_read -> response.serialize -> http.send
- Important tags/fields for spans: batch_id, batch_size, gpu_id, quantization_profile, kernel_version, kv_hit=true/false, token_range (start-end)
- Sampling policy (practical):
  * default: 5–10% random sampling (keeps storage reasonable)
  * deterministic full-sample triggers: any request with error, latency.end_to_end_p95 > 1200ms, tokens > 2048, or fallback.model_rate event
  * experimental: 100% sampling for canary tenants during rollout window (configurable per-tenant)

Session reconstruction checklist (how to go from alert -> single-request view)
1) From the alert, get the implicated route_name, time window, and top affected tenant(s).
2) Use request.count + error rate panel to find a candidate timestamp range (typically +-2m).
3) Open the probe & cohort heatmap and identify input-size bucket with largest delta.
4) Query traces with filters: route_name, tenant_id (if available), token_count_estimate bucket, sample_trigger in (error, high-latency) ordered by start_time desc.
5) If traces missing, check sampling budget and increase sample_trigger thresholds for a short window; meanwhile reconstruct from logs: correlate request_id -> batch_id -> gpu_id from runtime logs.

Dashboard panel design notes (cost-aware, compact):
- Keep row height small, use sparklines + single number + delta vs baseline. Avoid full tables except when needed.
- Use heatmap for token-size vs latency: x-axis token-size buckets (0-32,33-128,129-512,513-1024,1025-2048,>2048), y-axis percentile or median latency. Color by traffic weight to highlight rare but expensive buckets.
- Panel: "Model cost burn" = tokens.generated_per_request * price/unit (config var) -> show 1h moving sum and per-route anchor.
- Failure mode panel: stacked bar of error reasons (model OOM, infra 5xx, timeout, parse error). Prioritize tags that are actionable.

Investigation play: common root causes and quick checks
- Spike in queue_ms (scheduler backlog): check batch_size trend, recent autoscale events, GPU allocation (gpu_id saturating), and routing policy changes.
- Decode spike: correlate runtime.invoke p95 with kernel_version and quantization_profile. If new kernel rolled out, rollback or isolate canary.
- Rate-limited client: request.count drop with 429s; check rate-limit config and per-tenant quota.
- Fallback regressions: bump in fallback.model_rate after rollout -> inspect model_variant latency/quality tradeoff table and eval runs.

Instrumentation TODOs (short list for next sprint)
- Add token_count_estimate to request-level metric emission in ingress proxy (INF-10321).
- Add batch_size tag to scheduler spans and surface median batch_size per route in console.
- Implement deterministic trace forwarding for any request with tokens >2k or error.

Practical tips for low-cardinality dashboards
- Avoid tenant_id in high-cardinality panels; summarize by tenant tier (free/prod/enterprise) instead. Use drilldowns to tenant-specific views only for affected tenant.
- Precompute bucketed token-size metrics (so dashboards don't do heavy aggregation on the fly).
- Use materialized hourly aggregates for heatmaps that don't need second-level fidelity.

Links & references
- Confluence: instrumentation-workbench (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-9876 (workstream for compact dashboards)
- Example query snippets: stored in github PR (linked above)

Open questions and parking lot
- How aggressive should sampling be for low-traffic customers? (cost vs visibility tradeoff).
- Should we add a sampling credit system per-team to avoid noisy experiments consuming trace budget?
- Explore trace compression (flatten and trim repeated kernel traces) to save storage.

Notes to self (rapid thoughts)
- Build a "one-click session replay" that attaches the lightweight trace to the alert and auto-populates the session reconstruction panel. Huge UX win.
- Consider a small "probe job" that synthetic-runs common routes every minute across regions to keep baseline heatmaps fresh.

If you're reading this: add any missing panels that helped you debug last incident to the TODOs above (esp. queries). We'll iterate this doc during the next observability sprint.
